results.summary: This project is an interactive Morse Code learning game that presents letters on a 7-segment display and challenges users to input the correct Morse code pattern using a switch. The system provides immediate feedback and progresses through the English alphabet. It can be tested in simulation or on hardware. The design requires a 100 Hz clock.

This project is a gate test designed to allow users to test the effect of different logic gates. Users can turn different switches on/off, attempting to get a specific outcome, with some inputs and outputs interconnected between gates. External hardware such as switches and a single number LED display are required for testing. The design was created using Wokwi.

This design displays a bouncing ROOTS logo on a VGA monitor, accompanied by an animated color gradient kaleidoscope background. It requires a VGA monitor and a Tiny VGA Pmod for external hardware connection. The design operates on a 25.175 MHz clock. The pins are configured for VGA output including R, G, B, VSync, and HSync signals.

This project implements a multi-length, 2-tap and 4-tap Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) with hold and step functionality. The LFSR taps are produced via a length table selected by the number of taps, and a 'valid' signal indicates a valid configuration. Each clock cycle produces a new LFSR value, which can be held or stepped. Testing was performed using simulation with hand-generated test modules, and external hardware can be used to configure and observe the LFSR values.

Borg is a tiny GPU built around a RISC-V SoC (TinyQV) that renders a 10-frame animation of a rotating RGB triangle. The entire rendering process is self-contained within the firmware, eliminating the need for host-side rendering. Testing involves programming the firmware onto an FPGA, which then renders the animation and outputs PPM images. External hardware includes a QSPI PMOD and potentially a Raspberry Pi Debug Probe for FPGA development.

This chip implements a ternary-weight transformer language model that generates text in the style of Shakespeare, with the entire model baked into ROM. It processes int16 residuals as input and outputs int8 residuals, one token per transaction. The design uses a 5-lane arithmetic unit and a small, fixed-size memory for context. Testing requires a host microcontroller like the RP2350B to handle character tables and final output processing, or can be partially verified with a logic analyzer by observing debug signals.

This project implements a simplified 8-bit microprocessor inspired by the 6502 architecture, featuring a central ALU, registers, and a microcoded instruction decoder executing a subset of the 6502 instruction set. The design is intended for testing with robust strategies, though specific testing methodologies are detailed in the documentation. The processor operates on a 40 MHz clock and utilizes bidirectional pins for data and unidirectional pins for address output.

This project is a Morse code generator circuit for the alphabets J and R, utilizing a 4-bit synchronous counter with AND and OR gates to simulate Morse code dots and dashes. It can be tested by connecting a 7-segment display and changing inputs with a button to represent the Morse code for J (".---") and R (".-."). External hardware required includes a button, a 7-segment display, and a clock source.

DUMBRV is a simple RISC-V processor supporting the base RV32E instruction set and Zicond/Zbs extensions, operating on two SPI memories. It uses independent SPI ports for read-only instruction memory and read-write data memory, both requiring 2-byte addresses. The processor begins execution immediately from address 0x0. Testing involves connecting SPI flash/EEPROM and SPI RAM, and programming a test program that records and outputs GPIO sequences to verify SPI memory functionality. The design requires one 512Kbit ROM and one 512Kbit RAM.

This project is a potentially working random number generator that attempts to leverage the unstable state of a latch. The design includes multiple instances of the generator to increase the chances of success, with input pins allowing for selection and interconnection of outputs. When the freeze input is 0, outputs are expected to fluctuate randomly; setting it to 1 allows sampling of the generated values. The documentation notes that bias or constant values are possible outcomes due to the nature of the unstable latch.
